transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No, do not use it at all. A battery that has become hot enough to split its casing and swell is a serious fire hazard; lithium-ion cells can vent gas or ignite if damaged further. Please stop using the vacuum immediately and do not attempt to charge this battery again. You need to contact Shark Customer Support for a replacement under warranty (the IZ201UK typically has a 5-year guarantee on the battery). They will arrange for you to return the faulty unit safely. Do not throw it in household waste; follow their instructions for safe disposal of damaged batteries.
Ok, understood. It's currently leaning against the kitchen cupboards next to the tea towels, still clicked into the vacuum, and it has a faint chemical smell. Where should I put it?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Move it immediately to an open, non-flammable area away from anything that could burn—ideally outside on concrete or in a metal bin if you have one. Do not leave it next to tea towels or against cupboards. Please contact Shark Customer Support for a warranty replacement and follow their instructions for safe disposal of the damaged unit.

candidates: Swollen lithium-ion battery cell (internal short or degradation) (high)

reading.symptom: battery got really hot on charge and looks puffed up with plastic case split at the seam

plan: They asked: "Can I still use it till a new one comes?" - answer that first.

Safety: a battery hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "battery got really hot on charge and looks puffed up with plastic case split at the seam". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
